title: Learning Rate Scheduling Quiz
description: Test your understanding of learning rate scheduling

questions.question: What is the main benefit of learning rate scheduling?
options: It reduces memory usage during training
It allows fast initial progress while ensuring stable final convergence
It eliminates the need for gradient computation
It automatically selects the best optimizer
questions.explanation: Learning rate scheduling combines the benefits of high learning rates (fast initial progress) with low learning rates (stable final convergence) by starting high and gradually reducing.

questions.question: In a step learning rate schedule, what happens every 'step_size' iterations?
options: The learning rate increases by a factor of gamma
The learning rate is reset to the initial value
The learning rate is multiplied by gamma (typically < 1)
The learning rate becomes zero
questions.explanation: In step scheduling, the learning rate is multiplied by gamma (usually 0.1 to 0.5) every step_size iterations, creating a staircase-like decay pattern.

questions.question: What is a key advantage of cosine annealing over exponential decay?
options: It requires no hyperparameters
It provides smooth decay and reaches the minimum learning rate exactly at the end of training
It increases the learning rate over time
It works only with Adam optimizer
questions.explanation: Cosine annealing provides a smooth decay curve that reaches the minimum learning rate exactly when training ends, making it ideal when you know the total training duration.

questions.question: When is 'reduce on plateau' scheduling most useful?
options: When you know exactly how many iterations you'll train
When you want the learning rate to increase over time
When you don't know in advance when the loss will stop improving
When training very simple models
questions.explanation: Reduce on plateau is adaptive - it monitors actual training progress and reduces the learning rate when improvement stalls, making it useful when training dynamics are unknown.

questions.question: What is a potential problem with exponential decay scheduling?
options: It increases computational cost
The learning rate can become too small too quickly
It only works with SGD
It requires too many hyperparameters
questions.explanation: Exponential decay can reduce the learning rate too aggressively, making it very small early in training and slowing down convergence unnecessarily.

questions.question: What typically happens if you reduce the learning rate too early in training?
options: Training becomes unstable
The model overfits immediately
Convergence becomes unnecessarily slow
Memory usage increases
questions.explanation: Reducing the learning rate too early means you lose the benefit of fast initial progress, making convergence unnecessarily slow when larger steps would still be beneficial.

questions.question: What is learning rate warmup?
options: Gradually increasing the learning rate from a small value to the target value
Keeping the learning rate constant throughout training
Randomly changing the learning rate
Using different learning rates for different parameters
questions.explanation: Warmup gradually increases the learning rate from a very small initial value to the target learning rate over the first few iterations, helping with training stability.

questions.question: Which scheduling strategy is often recommended as a good starting point for most problems?
options: Exponential decay
Constant learning rate
Step scheduling
Polynomial decay
questions.explanation: Step scheduling is simple, effective, and works well for most problems. It's easy to understand, implement, and tune, making it a good starting point.
